summary: Esho Mikogami (1935–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He founded Indogaku Chibettogaku Kenkyū, served as president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997, and was a professor at Ryukoku University from circa 1974 to 2003.

Esho Sasaki (born 1937) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. His career includes serving as an associate professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

Esho Yamaguchi (born 1918) studied at Kyoto University and worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Ritsumeikan University and served as a professor at Osaka University from circa 1972 to 1982.

Ester Bianchi (born 1971) studied under Jean-Noël Robert and Alfredo Cadonna, earning PhDs from Ca' Foscari University and EPHE (~1999–2003). A Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar, she taught at Ca' Foscari and Florence, joining the University of Perugia in ~2007.
Ethan Kroll works in Indology and related fields. In 2012, he was attested as an editorial board member for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies and held a position at Baker McKenzie.
Etienne Vermeersch (1934–2019) was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University from circa 1953 to 1958. He later held a faculty post at Ghent University from 1967 to 1997.

Etsuaki Teraishi works in the fields of Indology and philosophy. Teraishi held a post as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and was a special researcher for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2001).

Eugen Hultzsch (1857–1927), an Indologist and linguist, studied at Leipzig and Vienna under Georg Bühler. He served as Government Epigraphist for Madras and the Government of India (~1886–1903) and later held the Sanskrit chair at the University of Halle (1903–1925).

Eugen Pander (1854–1894) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Polytechnikum Riga (~1872–1876) and served as a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan in 1881.
Eugen Prym (1843–1913) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1860 to 1863 and later held a post there from circa 1868 to 1913.

Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under August Schleicher from circa 1864 to 1868 and served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1872 to 1923.

Eugene Watson Burlingame (1876–1932) studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman in 1909, working in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was a Harrison Fellow at the University of Pennsylvania (~1913–1914), Johnston Scholar at Johns Hopkins (~1914–1917), and Lecturer on Pāli at Yale (~1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang studied under Wu Hung and John M. Rosenfield (~1990–1997) in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held a post at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997) before becoming Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art at Harvard (~1997).

Eugeni d'Ors (1881–1954) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona (~1897–1903) and Universidad Central (~1903–1905). He later held a post at Universidad Central from circa 1927 to 1953.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz (1901–1981) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying at the University of Lviv (~1919–1928), he held posts there (~1934–1939), at Nicolaus Copernicus University (~1945–1953), and as head of Indology at the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf (1801–1852), an Indologist and specialist in Iranian and Buddhist studies, studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He served as secretary of the Société Asiatique (attested 1826, 1829, 1832) and taught at the Collège de France from 1832 to 1852.
Eugène Jacquet (1811–1838) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from circa 1828 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from circa 1832 to 1838.

Eugène Obermiller (1901–1935) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1921–1925) and Dondub Buddhayin (1929), later serving as Section Secretary at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1935).

Eugène Tisserant (1884–1972) worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Lycee Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1905–1908), and École du Louvre (~1906–1908).

Eun Hino (born 1981) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a master's degree at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2006). Hino held a post as a project researcher there (~2011–2014) and became an assistant professor at Musashino University circa 2014.
